title: Manjari 6. Return to Gauda and Again to Vrindavana
html:
Lokanatha entrusts Narottama to Srinivasa; the farewell circuit of Vraja; Jiva secretly equips the travellers through the merchants of Agra; Govinda's garland; Narottama at Garanhati and his kirtana; Srinivasa at Yajigrama: Ramachandra Kaviraja, the "second eye"; the marriage; the second journey to Vrindavana; Gopala Bhatta makes Srinivasa adhikari of Radha-ramana

[p. 77]

Sri-raga.

1Bow down to Sri Krishna Chaitanya with His associates —
the limit of compassion, besides whom there is no other.

2Begging them Himself, He distributes the highest goal to the fallen;
the name "Purifier of the fallen" has now come true.

3I shall tell of one more wonder —
how Sri Thakura Mahashaya set out for the land of Gauda.

[p. 78]

4Sri Lokanatha Gosani had long
intended to send him to Gauda.

5The three things he forbade him to accept —
that (applied) only to Gauda: he knew it by insight.

6Living here, (Narottama) would avoid those three things of himself,
dependent on the feet of all the Gosvamis.1

7Now a great love had arisen between him
and Sri Acharya Thakura — this (Lokanatha) knew at heart.

8He himself loves him very much;
and so, sending him alone, he foresees various hindrances.

9He knows in his mind: sooner or later, one day,
he will certainly have to go to Gauda.

10Therefore, calling him to a secluded place,
he speaks his heart, moved with mercy:

11"Listen, I shall tell you what I think.
Mahaprabhu spread the sankirtana;

12it cannot be relished without the land of Gauda —
service to Radha and Krishna together with service to the Vaishnavas."

13Thakura Mahashaya is greatly eager for kirtana,
eager to manifest service to Sri Krishna and the Vaishnavas;

14this thought had always been with him, and now — from the guru's lips;
on first hearing it he was very glad.

15But then, remembering the bliss of Vrindavana,
he began to speak, weeping and weeping:

[p. 79]

16"Prabhu, here I serve you,
I see Gopala, Govinda and Gopinatha,

17I live in Vrindavana; from the lips of all of you
I hear of the pastimes of Radha and Krishna and rejoice in darshana.

18Let me stay for now; when my heart is ready,
I shall come at once and tell you."

19Gosani says: "Since you must go in any case,
I shall be anxious if you go later.

20With the Acharya you will not grieve,
and I, entrusting you to him, shall be happy."

21Hearing this, he fell silent.
The next day Acharya Thakura came.

22Gosani asked him for a definite answer:
"What have you decided about going to the land of Gauda?"

23He says: "Having circumambulated Sri Govardhana,
the chief places of Vraja, the twelve forests,

24I shall come back and certainly go to Gauda;
there is no doubt of it — that is my secret."

25Hearing this, Gosani called Thakura (Narottama);
with his left hand he took Acharya Thakura's hand,

26with his right — Thakura Narottama's hand,
and placed it in Acharya Thakura's hand.

27With tears, faltering, he speaks sweet words:
"You will cherish my Narottama as your life.

[p. 80]

28And he will see you as like me.
Do what pleases me."

29Hearing this, both bowed down to Gosani;
Gosani raised them both and embraced them.

30Thakura bowed down to Acharya Thakura;
Acharya Thakura raised him and embraced him.

31Both thrilled, streams of tears from their eyes;
seeing this, Gosani felt boundless happiness.

32Rising in the morning, both bathed and so on
and took leave of the Gosanis everywhere.

33Sri Jiva Gosani gave them as companion
a knowledgeable Vaishnava to show them all the places.

34In the evening they stopped at Sri Madhupuri;
the next morning, having bathed at Madhuvana,

35having seen Talavana and Kumudavana there,
they spent that night with joyful hearts.

36At dawn, having seen Bahulavana,
coming to Radha-kunda they bathed and so on.

37Offering dandavat obeisances to Sri Dasa Gosani,
they rested there that night.

38In order they told Gosani
the whole story; hearing it, Gosani rejoiced at heart.

39In talk of Krishna (the night) passed like a moment;
rising in the morning, they bathed and performed remembrance.

[p. 81]

40Keeping Sri Kunda on their right, Govardhana
they set out to circumambulate, their hearts overflowing.

41The names always on their lips: Radha, Krishna, Govinda;
seeing the places of the pastimes and the service — what bliss!

42Tears, trembling, thrills and other transformations of bhava —
how much shall I write? It is far too extensive.

43Relishing the secret of each place, both
fall to the ground, absorbed (in bhava).

44After a while, regaining awareness, they hurry on again,
go to another place of the pastimes and receive darshana.

45In one place I have written, merely pointing the direction;
know that everywhere it was the same.

46Having circumambulated Govardhana, they returned
and spent that night at the feet of Dasa Gosani.

47In many ways Gosani showed them mercy —
who is there who could describe it?

48How they wept at parting —
telling of that sorrow, I feel great anguish.

49From there, walking on and on, they came to Paramandala2
and, seeing Adi-Badri, bowed down.

50Spending the night there, in the morning they went to Kamyavana
and saw all the places in order.

51From there they came to Vrishabhanupura;
looking at everything, streams of tears flow from their eyes.

[p. 82]

52At that time there was neither service nor temple there —
therefore I have not written about it.

53Spending that night and seeing Prema-sarovara,
they rejoiced at the darshana of Sanketa.

54Spending that night there, they went to Nandagrama,
saw the king of Vraja with his associates and bowed down.

55In Pavana-sarovara they bathed and so on;
the bliss that arose cannot be told.

56All around they saw the places of the pastimes;
in the morning, walking on, they came to Khadiravana.

57From there they went to the village called Yavat;
seeing the places of the pastimes, they rested there.

58In the morning, when they saw Kokila-vana —
the bliss that came I cannot describe.

59Having seen Bathain, they see Charana-pahari;
seeing the footprints and other marks, they were very glad.

60Their companion shows them from the hill
all the villages there are around.

61Having seen the secret (of the pastime) there, they went to Dahi-gaon;
that night, in happy talk of Krishna, they spent there.

62In the morning, going to the village of Kotimani,
they found bliss in seeing the kadamba grove.

63From there, walking on, they came to Shesha-shayi;
in the kunda called Kshira-samudra they bathed and performed remembrance.

[p. 83]

64They received the darshana of Sri Lakshmi-Narayana
and spent that night there as well.

65The son of the king of Vraja performs the Shesha-shayi pastime —
telling of this, both relished happiness.

66From there they came to the village of Khayra;
having seen Sanjhoi, they rested there.

67Then, having seen Ujani,
they went to rest at Khelana-vana.

68Then Ramaghat, Akshaya-vata,
Gopighat they saw near the Yamuna.

69That day, coming to Chira-ghat, they stayed there;
the next morning they arrived at Nanda-ghat.

70Having bathed and so on, they went on joyfully;
crossing the Sri Yamuna, they went to Bhadravana.

71Then, having bathed at Bhandiravana,
they went to Belavana, deeply absorbed in prema.

72Seeing the forest on the Yamuna's bank, they rejoiced;
seeing the beauty of Vrindavana on the far bank, they were amazed.

73That day they stayed there in the joy of darshana;
the next day they rested at Lohavana.

74Manasa-sarovara lies within Vrindavana;
the Yamuna flows to the north of that lake —

75therefore I have not mentioned it in the account of the circuit.
In the morning they took the road along the Yamuna.

[p. 84]

76Walking on and on, reaching the village of Raval,
seeing the birthplace of Sri Radhika —

77the bliss that came could not be contained in their bodies;
they stayed right there — for prema they could not walk.

78Then they set out for Gokula;
seeing its beauty, they rested at Mahavana.

79There, seeing Nanda's house and the various places of the pastimes —
what happiness they felt, only they are witness.

80Then at Mathura, at Vishranti — midday;
spending the day there, in the morning they go to Vrindavana.

81There — the meeting with all the Gosanis.
They considered how to send them to the land of Gauda.

82They would like to send them with money and provisions —
but no one accepts anything; what can be done?

83Then to a merchant whose carts were going to Agra
Sri Jiva Gosani said in secret:

84"Whatever books and other things Acharya Mahashaya has,
take this load and go quickly.

85There, lodging him in your own house,
pay the carter whatever the cart costs.

86Whatever he needs for the road,
give it all together — so that I may be pleased.

87I know: do not tell him this —
knowing it comes from me, he will never accept."

[p. 85]

88That merchant (said): "I have always prayed,
but I was never given an order to serve."

89Now, receiving the order, he was filled with joy
and took on himself the charge of sending them to Gauda.

90The next day he said to Acharya Thakura:
"Be merciful, come with me to Agra.

91There we are many merchants;
whatever is to be decided we shall decide there."

92Moved by his humility, Thakura agreed
and went and told Gosani everything.

93Hearing it, Gosani was glad at heart
and then handed over all the books —

94some old, some newly copied;
he had kept them ready beforehand.

95Having handed over everything, in boundless bliss,
they began to think of the farewell.

96Sri Acharya Thakura and Sri Thakura Mahashaya
took leave of everyone, bowing humbly.

97What befell them everywhere at the leave-taking —
for sorrow I cannot describe it in full.

98Mana-sarovara, Kali-hrada and the rest —
all the places they saw in the rapture of prema;

99seeing the samadhis of all the Gosanis,
they wept long, rolling on the ground.

[p. 86]

100They went to all the temples and received darshana;
at the parting both were in great agitation.

101Prasada sandal, cloth, tulasi buds,
the dust of the rasa, the dust of (the Vaishnavas') feet — they filled bags.

102When, at the parting, (they stood) before Sri Govinda,
they gazed fixedly at His moonlike face,

103wiping away again and again the streams of tears;
who could describe that yearning?

104At that moment the garland on Govinda's Sri body,
under the weight of great compassion, slipped and fell.

105The pujari brought the garland and gave it to Acharya Thakura;
receiving the garland of mercy, his prema doubled.

106Again and again he rises, falls, offers dandavat obeisances —
tears, trembling, thrills and the other transformations of bhava.

107Clasping everyone's feet, he wept long;
the hearts of all who were there melted.

108Thus some time passed;
the curtain was drawn at Govinda's door.

109Then all together calmed him
and, gradually saying everything, bade him farewell.

110With the greatest difficulty taking courage,
stricken with grief, they reached Agra.

111There all the merchants, gathering together,
humbly hired a cart for them.

[p. 87]

112The books are many — the baggage cannot go with them;
understanding this, they arranged everything:

113whatever was needed for the journey,
clothing, vessels — all that was required on the way —

114they gave everything; and then, with royal passes,
each escorted them to the border of his own domain.

115Thus by degrees they came to the land of Gauda.3
I shall tell briefly, as a sutra, some particulars of it.

116Sri Thakura Mahashaya went to Garanhat;
there he carried out the guru's order.

117He relished kirtana in countless special ways;
and the splendour of the service — how much of it can be told?

118His service to the Vaishnavas and Gosanis is wonderful to hear;
practising it himself, he showed the essence of bhakti.

119Acharya Thakura's disciple is Bara Kaviraja Thakura:
with him (Narottama's) love grew immensely.

120The perfection of that love is impossible among (ordinary) people:
hearing of it, the hearts of all beings melt.

121Following his (Narottama's) dancing and relishing,
the "Garanhati kirtana" became famous.4

122Ceaseless absorption in bhava, especially in kirtana —
as if prema incarnate were walking about by itself.

123All the transformations of bhava of a single day —
write from birth on, and still you would not reach the end.

[p. 88]

124Sri Acharya Thakura lived at Yajigrama;
he accepted many disciples — Sri Ramachandra Kaviraja and others.

125When he made Bara Kaviraja his disciple,
he then told him this secret:

126"One deeply feeling, skilled in beauty and virtues,
like you — I obtained one eye in Vrindavana.

127One-eyed I have been for many days;
today the most skilful Creator has given me a second eye."5

128Saying this, he drew him onto his lap
and bathed him with the tears of his eyes.

129Kaviraja Thakura, receiving the embrace of mercy,
lost consciousness, his heart melted with prema.

130A single bhava is deep as millions of oceans —
it cannot be understood; what wise man could describe it?

131Seeing it, all the bhagavatas present weep;
their bodies are filled with bliss beyond containing.

132First of all he taught him all the books
and infused into that all his own power.

133Beauty, virtues, Vaishnava character, the limit of learning —
the Creator joined them all in making him.

134Before Sri Acharya Thakura he does not speak a word,
although he is fit to speak.

135Whatever question Acharya Thakura asks,
he answers it most sweetly.

[p. 89]

136Whatever order he receives, he never acts otherwise,
not considering his own good or harm.

137"My own arm" — so the Prabhu calls him again and again,
finding occasion, with boundless satisfaction.

138When one hears talk of Radha and Krishna from his lips —
not to speak of people, even stones melt.

139With all the mahantas there are in Sri Gauda
he met and conversed in private.

140Hearing of the passing of Sri Vishnupriya-jiu,
he wept long, beating his head.

141In many ways they tried to have him marry —
Thakura Sarakara and the others;

142at everyone's insistence he married.6
He taught many people the books of bhakti,

143living by the essence of siddhanta and the essence of rasa;
he made known to all the path of raganuga, above everything.

144He carried out Sri Gosani-jiu's order;
thus he lived there for some time.

145His longing for Vrindavana grew;
again, leaving everything, he set out.

146By degrees he came to Sri Vrindavana;
first of all he received the darshana of Sri Bhatta Gosani.

147He offered dandavat obeisances, and he embraced him;
in the rapture of prema guru and disciple both lost consciousness.

[p. 90]

148Composing himself with difficulty, seated on his seat,
(Bhatta Gosani) asked all the news of the land of Gauda,

149and gave him the darshana of Sri Radha-ramana;
seeing Him, (Srinivasa)'s bliss and tears doubled.

150Again he asked: "Have you married?"
He says: "I did not do it (of myself) — why do you ask?"7

151Then he received the darshana of Sri Jiva Gosani,
offered dandavat obeisances and spoke humble words with tears.

152Gosani, overcome with prema, embraced him,
having found reunion after a long time,

153and gave him the darshana of Sri Radha-Damodara;
both were overpowered by rapture, their hearts overflowing.

154Growing calm, he again asked all the news;
Thakura told of the state of the land of Gauda:

155the teaching of the scriptures of bhakti, the spreading of bhakti.
Hearing it, Gosani rejoiced at heart.

156Then, seeing Sri Govinda, Gopala and Gopinatha,
(Srinivasa) deemed his life fulfilled.

157Having seen and bowed to the adhikari Gosani and everyone,
he partook of maha-prasada.

158Seeing Sri Lokanatha Gosani,
he offered dandavat obeisances, absorbed in prema.

159Gosani, with tears, embraced him with love;
then (Srinivasa) tells about Sri Thakura Narottama:

[p. 91]

160"In the service of Krishna and the Vaishnavas, in detachment from worldly things,
he fully carries out your order."

161Hearing of the relishing of sankirtana, (Lokanatha) floats in bliss;
remembering his virtues, he weeps aloud.

162And, meeting all the mahantas,
he spent some days in great happiness:

163bathing in the Sri Yamuna, darshana of all the Thakuras,
hearing of the pastimes from the Gosanis in all the places.

164The happiness of a single day I cannot tell.
Then Bhatta Gosani, showing mercy to Thakura,

165said: "Having considered it in my mind, I have made you
the adhikari of Radha-ramana.

166In my absence — all authority;
the whole burden of the service — is yours."

167"From today I have so decided,"
he told Sri Jiva Gosani and everyone.

168Hearing it, all rejoiced at heart:
"You have judged worthily, by the essence of sound reasoning."8

169Thus many days passed in bliss.
Meanwhile there Sri Ishvari-jiu grew anxious.

170She called Sri Bara Kaviraja Thakura
and in private told him all the sorrow of her heart:

171"It would be well for you to go to Vrindavana:
it is fitting to find out once how he is."

[p. 92]

172You wanted to go to Sri Vrindavana anyway —
good: two tasks have come together."

173Receiving the order, he was overjoyed;
going home, he set out with everyone's consent.

174Kaviraja Thakura is very delicate of body;
he walks slowly, as far as he can each day.

175Some days later he arrived in Vrindavana
and first of all met Bhatta Gosani.

176He told him all the news;
as soon as he heard it, he felt boundless sorrow at heart:

177"He told me such an untruth!
Such conduct is never fitting for a disciple."

178At once they sent for Acharya Thakura;
coming, he first saw Kaviraja Thakura.

179He offered dandavat obeisances; Thakura grew anxious
and then came before Bhatta Gosani.

180Gosani says: "You told me such an untruth!
What dharma did you see in it? I want to understand your reasoning."

181Thakura says: "Worship of your feet,
the darshana of Gopala, Govinda, Gopinatha,

182the company of Sri Jiva Gosani, life in Vrindavana,
the joy of talk of Krishna with everyone —

183so much is gained by a single untrue word;
out of this greed I said it, with an abashed heart."

[p. 93]

184Saying this, Thakura offered dandavat obeisances;
Bhatta Gosani, laughing and laughing, embraced him:

185"Even by lying you have won me over;
there is no fault in it — so I tell you.

186But the adhikari of Sri Radha-ramana —
unless he is a renunciant, I cannot make him so."

187"This great sorrow cannot be told;
I have understood the Lord's will — what can be done?"9

188Then Sri Acharya Thakura, taking Kaviraja Thakura
everywhere with him, joyfully showed him all the holy places.

189At that time there was such a rule:
one who came having married could not stay (in Vrindavana).

190Hearing this, all gave him leave (to go);
it was decided that he would go to the land of Gauda.

191That time Sri Vyasa had come with Acharya Thakura;
he wished to be initiated by Sri Jiva Gosani.

192He says: "This Acharya Mahashaya is the same as I;
there is no doubt of it," he said for certain.

193In private he revealed the whole secret to him
and, himself present, had him made (Srinivasa's) disciple.10

194Sri Gopinatha Pujari is Acharya Thakura's spiritual (brother);
Acharya Thakura had him made adhikari.11

195He had a great friendship with him;
therefore he made that request to Gosani.

[p. 94]

196Pujari Gosani to his brother's son,
Sri Harinatha Gosani, gave the authority (of adhikari).

197Some days later his father came —
named Damodara Gosani, giver of joy to all.

198With him came his two sons —
Gosani Harirama and the one named Mathuradasa.

199Even today the descendants of the three brothers are the adhikaris.
I have written briefly — it cannot be told in full.

200How they obtained the authority
is very lengthy; I have told the essence.

201Some days later, taking Kaviraja along,
(Srinivasa) went round Vraja, rejoicing.

202Then, taking leave as before — to the land of Gauda;
some days later they arrived and entered it.

203With Sri Jiva Gosani lived Sri Shyamananda Gosani;
him he sent along with Acharya Thakura

204and said: "Through you in the land of Utkala
many will be delivered — know it for certain."

205Formerly his name was Duhkhini Krishnadasa;
afterwards this name became known.

206His body is dark and beautiful, he is immersed in the happiness of prema;
knowing this, Sri Jiva with his own lips gave him the name.12

207His boundless virtues are known to the world;
taking his name, one becomes dear to Gaura's devotees.

[p. 95]

208And taking these two — Vyasa and him — Acharya Thakura
came to the land of Gauda together with Kaviraja.

209As before, he spread the scriptures of bhakti;
many became his disciples — Vira Hambira and others.

210In Vishnupura (the king) built him a house
and served him in every way.13

211Thus for some time he lived there;
again the wish to go to Vrindavana grew.

212His eldest son — Vrindavana-vallabha Thakura,
and with him Bara Kaviraja, in great bliss.

213With everyone's consent he came to Vrindavana
and, as before, met with everyone.

214On the way he made an agreement with Kaviraja:
"Whoever first fills and brings the water pot —

215with whatever (water) one wishes to perform (ablutions),
let him use it from his own vessel — this is my order."14

216Wonderful is Kaviraja Thakura's conduct:
whatever order he receives, he carries it out without fail.

217In Vrindavana all the Vaishnavas, hearing (of this),
asked him: "What did you do on the way? Tell us.

218The elder (guru) brings it and the disciple uses it —
nowhere have we heard of such a rule of scripture."

219He says: "My Prabhu is here;
ask him — he will explain the reason."

[p. 96]

220Then all asked Acharya Thakura;
hearing it, Acharya Thakura laughed:

221"Ask him himself," he said.
They say: "We asked — he did not tell."

222Then Acharya Thakura says: "Tell him:
'We asked your gurudeva how it was,

223and he said: ask Kaviraja.'
Then he will tell — know it for certain."

224So they asked Kaviraja Thakura;
knowing it to be the guru's order, he cited scriptural proof:

225Thus in the agamas:
"The order of the guru is not to be deliberated upon."15

226Hearing this, all fell silent.
But these words are for the qualified:

227one who can act so everywhere will be delivered;
but if he fails in even one place, he is merely an offender.

228Bara Kaviraja's brother is named Govinda Kaviraja.
I shall tell briefly something of his virtues.

229He sent his songs to Sri Jiva Gosani;
hearing them, the devotees' lives are refreshed.

230Gosani with his associates relished them;
the prema that grew cannot be written.

231But when (Jiva) sent a reply,
a companion of Sri Jiva wrote (a verse) in it;

[p. 97]

232in one shloka he expressed all their relishing —
consider and see, applying your own minds.

233Thus the shloka: "The fragrance of the garland of poems connected with Krishna, borne by the cool breezes from the sandal mountain, Sri Govinda, king of poets, intoxicating the bees that cling to the feet of the wish-fulfilling tree, Srimad Jiva, has caused wonder to all in the forest of Vraja — what more (is there to say)?"16

234Thus, as before, after staying some days,
he left for the land of Gauda by order.

235Three times he went to Vrindavana and back;
of this I have told something briefly.

236He carried out Sri Gosani-jiu's order:
everywhere he established the treasure of prema for Radha and Krishna,

237he spread all the books of bhakti-rasa,
in countless special ways he relished sankirtana.

238The service of the shalagrama named Sri Vamshivadana —
the rule he established for it,

239hear it: whoever bathes first,
if he does not perform that service, incurs a penalty.

240Sometimes Thakurani herself, sometimes a son,
sometimes the servant-disciple living in the house;

241with tulasi, sandal paste, various flowers and so on
they serve Thakura calmly.

[p. 98]

242Then Thakurani, in the pot (kept) in Thakura's room,
cooks (rice) with two or four vegetable dishes;

243lifting the pot, she offers Thakura the bhoga,
then, removing the bhoga, gives (Him) mukhavasa

244and with great joy lays (Him) to rest.
Then (food) is cooked in the prasada pot.

245Vaishnavas are constantly coming and going;
at midday, gathering together, they partake of maha-prasada.

246Many vegetable dishes are prepared beforehand;
as soon as anyone comes, rice is cooked.

247Thus, when one prahara of the night has passed,
again, having made the evening (offering), they clear the vessels.

248In time Sri Hemalata Thakurani Mahashaya
began to strive for the manifestation of (a new) service;

249knowing her yearning from her many efforts,
(Srinivasa) gave the order: "Serve (Him) carefully."

250Receiving the order, she manifested the Sri Deity,
and, having bathed (His body), installed Him in the temple.

251(This is) the service of Acharya Thakura's own guru:
after His name (the Deity) was named Sri Radha-ramana.17

252All the Vaishnavas came — a great festival;
what they did — what can I say? It was all beyond this world.

253Bara Kaviraja Thakura lived in Sri Kheturi
with Sri Thakura (Narottama), in great friendship.

[p. 99]

254For Sri Acharya Thakura there
they built a special house and carefully kept it:

255no one enters it, the door stays shut;
when Acharya Thakura comes, he stays in that house.

256Every day both (friends) come to that house
and offer dandavat obeisances, with the rapture of prema in their hearts.

257Acharya Thakura lives in Sri Yajigrama,
sometimes rests in Vishnupura, sometimes in Kheturi.

258Thakura Mahashaya and Bara Kaviraja Thakura —
with both of them flows the relishing of rasa, a flood of prema.

259Kaviraja Thakura and Thakura Mahashaya, for the Kartika vows,
always come to Yajigrama for darshana.

260Keeping the vow on the bank of the river Mahananda,
they humbly say something to him:

261"When we return to Kheturi again,
then we shall carry you on our heads to this place."18

262After Kaviraja Thakura's departure, Thakura Mahashaya
used to come in this way to Acharya Thakura's abode.

263Then all of Thakura's (Srinivasa's) sons departed (from the world);
again, for the continuance of the line, they urged him.

264All the mahantas together had him married again;
then a son was born — Sri Govinda-gati Thakura.

265He was born by the blessing of Sri Virabhadra Gosani;
at this everyone together rejoiced.19

[p. 100]

266There is a second pada of Sri Acharya Thakura,
in which we obtain his full shelter:

267Radha speaks to Sri Vishakha of Her anuraga —
the extract of rasa that captivates the hearts of rasikas.

268Here is the pada: "You always keep me in your lap, you cover me with your cloth; outside you is a foreign land. There is no one on earth I may call my own — and such a desire in such a wretch! Friend, what more shall I say at your feet? For one whose heart is attached to that unattainable one, death alone is the cure. (Refrain.) Whatever I do, I cannot steady myself; night and day do not pass. All the relatives in the house are my enemies: what shall I do, what way out can there be?"20

269This pada is the life of those who have taken his shelter;
the treasure of hearing, or an ornament for the ears,

270or the essence of rasa, a mine of anuraga,
the limit of sweetness, or a heavenly river of nectar.

271So I have told of his play of prema,
hearing of which devotees gain firm faith.

272Those whose all-in-all is Sri Rupa with his family —
for their joy this pastime is proclaimed.

[p. 101]

273Wishing to describe this connection, the gurus and the rest,
Manohara Dasa tells the Anuraga-valli.

Thus ends, in the Srimad Anuraga-valli, the sixth manjari, called "The Play of Prema of Srimad Acharya Thakura".

Notes

  1. The sense of the couplet (especially the word "parachin") is unclear; translated by sense: in Vrindavana, under the care of the Gosvamis, Narottama would not be threatened by marriage and Bengali food.
  2. "Paramandala" — so in the edition; apparently a village in Vraja near Adi-Badri.
  3. The theft of the books by the robbers of King Vira Hambira in Vishnupura, told in detail by the Prema-vilasa (7), the Karnananda (6), the Narottama-vilasa and the Bhakti-ratnakara, is not mentioned here: the journey to Gauda is described as uneventful.
  4. Garanhati (Garanhat) — the district of Kheturi, Narottama's homeland; "garanhati" is the style of kirtana introduced by Narottama.
  5. The first "eye" is Narottama, the second Ramachandra Kaviraja; the image is known only from the Anuraga-valli.
  6. Thakura Sarakara — Narahari Sarakara Thakura of Srikhanda. Srinivasa's marriage at the insistence of the Vaishnavas also appears in the Prema-vilasa (16), where news of it is brought to Gopala Bhatta in Vrindavana.
  7. Literally the answer is "I did not do it"; the sense is apparently "I married not of my own will but at the Vaishnavas' insistence", cf. 141–142.
  8. According to the Anuraga-valli, Gopala Bhatta makes Srinivasa adhikari of Radha-ramana; according to the Prema-vilasa (25), he entrusted the service of Radha-ramana to Gopinatha.
  9. Apparently the words of Gopala Bhatta. Srinivasa's lie, his repentance and forgiveness form an episode known only from the Anuraga-valli.
  10. Sri Vyasa — apparently Vyasa Chakravarti (cf. Karnananda 5), a disciple of Srinivasa; that he wished to be initiated by Jiva and was directed by him to Srinivasa is known only from the Anuraga-valli.
  11. I.e. adhikari of Radha-ramana in place of Srinivasa himself. Cf. Prema-vilasa 25.507: Gopala Bhatta entrusted the service of Radha-ramana to Gopinatha. What follows (Harinatha, Damodara, Harirama, Mathuradasa) is the tradition of the family of the Radha-ramana gosvamis.
  12. Shyamananda ("the bliss of Shyama"). According to the Prema-vilasa (12), Jiva gave him the name after Duhkhi Krishnadasa found Radha's nupura; here it is for his "dark and beautiful" body and his prema.
  13. Vira Hambira's initiation and his service to Srinivasa are told in detail in the Prema-vilasa (7), the Karnananda and the Bhakti-ratnakara, where they are preceded by the theft of the books.
  14. The sense of the rule is unclear; apparently Srinivasa told Ramachandra to use without hesitation water that the guru himself sometimes brought — hence the Vaishnavas' question (218).
  15. The saying "ājñā gurūṇāṁ hy avicāraṇīyā" (cf. Raghuvamsha 14.46).
  16. A reply verse from Vrindavana to Govinda Kaviraja's songs; cf. Jiva's letters in the Karnananda (5) and the Bhakti-ratnakara, where Jiva confers on Govinda the title "Kaviraja". The text of the verse is corrupt in places in the edition; the translation is approximate.
  17. I.e. Hemalata's Deity is named after Gopala Bhatta's Radha-ramana, the Deity of Srinivasa's guru.
  18. The sense is unclear; possibly "we shall carry you on our heads to Kheturi".
  19. Virabhadra (Virachandra) — Nityananda's son. Srinivasa's second marriage and the birth of Govinda-gati also appear in the Prema-vilasa and the Karnananda; for Virabhadra's blessing cf. Prema-vilasa 25.
  20. A pada of Srinivasa; Radha's words to Vishakha. Her anuraga is the highest prema, not worldly passion.
